summary: A closed GitHub issue from the archived docker-archive/swarm-library-image repository, titled 'Build Swarm image and Run error : no such file or directory'. User chengjingtao built a locally modified Swarm binary into a Docker image, and the container failed to start with a 'no such file or directory' error, while the official Swarm image and a hello-world binary ran fine. Maintainer vieux explained the Dockerfile uses FROM scratch, so the binary must be compiled statically; the user confirmed this fixed the problem and the issue was closed on Nov 13, 2015.
one_line: GitHub issue where a locally built Docker Swarm image failed with 'no such file or directory' until the binary was compiled statically.
key_facts: The issue is #5 in the docker-archive/swarm-library-image repository and was titled 'Build Swarm image and Run error : no such file or directory'.
The issue was opened by chengjingtao on Nov 4, 2015.
The user built a modified Swarm executable into a Docker image tagged chengjt/swarm:local.
The container failed with the error 'System error: no such file or directory' even though running the executable directly worked.
The official Swarm image and a simple hello world program renamed to swarm both built and ran normally.
The user reported Docker version 1.8.3, build f4bf5c7.
The user reported go version go1.4.2 linux/amd64.
Maintainer vieux replied on Nov 4, 2015 that the binary needed to be compiled statically.
vieux noted the Dockerfile uses FROM scratch, so the container contains nothing, not even libc.
chengjingtao replied on Nov 13, 2015 that the static build worked.
The issue was closed as completed by chengjingtao on Nov 13, 2015.
The repository was archived by its owner on Nov 10, 2020 and is read-only.
